name: Kelela
label: Warp
lede: She quit telemarketing in 2012 with two songs recorded and gave her first mixtape away free. A decade later, a mostly Berlin-made album landed at No. 17 on Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2023.

eras.title: From a Gaithersburg violin to a telemarketing headset
eras.text: Kelela Mizanekristos grew up in the Maryland suburbs on R&B, jazz and Björk, sang prog metal in D.C., and moved to Los Angeles two years before she walked out of a telemarketing job.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kelela · Wikipedia: Take Me Apart
years.h: Born in D.C., raised in Gaithersburg on violin and R&B
years.p: Kelela is the only child of Ethiopian American parents. She played violin from fourth grade and sang in her school choir.
years.xp: Wikipedia gives her birth name as Kelela Mizanekristos and her birth date as June 4, 1983. In 2017 she described herself as a black woman and second-generation Ethiopian-American who grew up in the burbs listening to R&B, jazz and Björk.

years.h: She finishes at Magruder, then sings jazz standards at American University
years.p: After Magruder High School in 2001 she went to Montgomery College, then transferred to American University, where she sang standards in local cafés.

years.src: Rolling Stone · The Ringer · Wikipedia: Kelela
years.h: Before R&B, she fronts a prog metal band
years.p: After meeting [[Tosin Abasi|9edadf07-e3a3-48b4-bff0-6a5c04298f5d]], Kelela joined the indie band Dizzy Spells and sang prog metal.
years.xp: Rolling Stone's 2023 profile places her in D.C.'s indie and punk scenes in the Myspace era, after open mic nights in college. The Ringer's 2017 profile says she sang jazz, metal and classic R&B after school before settling on R&B.

years.h: Kelela moves to Los Angeles
years.p: L.A. is where she would meet the producers who built her first mixtape. She now lives between Los Angeles and London.

years.h: She quits telemarketing with two songs in the can
years.p: In November 2012 Kelela left the job to make a mixtape. Two songs were already recorded.

eras.title: Free, and made for the club
eras.text: Fade to Mind and Night Slugs made warped, bass-heavy club music, mostly without singers. Kelela became the voice of that scene.

years.h: One guest spot on Teengirl Fantasy's "EFX" opens the Fade to Mind door
years.p: Kelela sang on "EFX" from Teengirl Fantasy's Tracer, which led her to Prince William of Fade to Mind. In May she appeared on [[Kingdom|2ae5ac16-1d41-464e-8fac-e856d91dd822]]'s "Bank Head".
years.xp: Prince William introduced her to the Fade to Mind sound and to its London sister label, Night Slugs. The Guardian's Harriet Gibsone later described Cut 4 Me as an experiment for the production team, the first time it had put vocals on its club tracks.

years.cap: Kelela at Broccoli City Festival, Washington, D.C.
years.src: Wikipedia: Cut 4 Me · Mixmag · Wikipedia: Kelela
yt: "Enemy", Boiler Room x adidas Originals Madrid
years.h: Cut 4 Me is free, and Pitchfork calls it Best New Music
years.p: Thirteen tracks on Fade to Mind, with beats from [[Kingdom|2ae5ac16-1d41-464e-8fac-e856d91dd822]], [[Nguzunguzu|de7d7191-5ca6-4e19-a69e-006a09a63df2]], [[Bok Bok|7bfc0474-c3bd-400e-bfb6-d1c66823c13d]], [[Girl Unit|a2be751d-53a5-491b-a565-80c9c3c39304]] and [[Jam City|1017c0b1-8219-4527-bc09-b32991bb8748]], released as a free SoundCloud download.
years.xp:
Kelela told Mixmag the tape held her first 20 completed songs, written when she was 30. The Guardian ranked it seventh among the albums of 2013, according to Wikipedia. Pitchfork called it "an ambitiously catchy record as well as being an aesthetically ambitious one."

A deluxe edition arrived April 6, 2015, adding an interlude and eight remixes. One of its tracks, "Go All Night", also turned up on Solange Knowles's Saint Heron compilation.

years.h: She posts "The High" herself, then sings on Bok Bok's "Melba's Call"
years.p: "The High" is a song from DJ Kitty Cash's Love the Free mixtape; Kelela put it out on February 4. [[Bok Bok|7bfc0474-c3bd-400e-bfb6-d1c66823c13d]]'s "Melba's Call", with her vocal, followed on March 5.

eras.title: Four years to a debut
eras.text: Kelela signed with Warp, released an EP that told a breakup in reverse, and took four years over her debut album while Solange, Danny Brown and Gorillaz called.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hallucinogen (EP) · Wikipedia: Kelela · The Ringer
years.h: Hallucinogen tells a relationship backwards
years.p: Warp and Cherry Coffee Music released the EP, produced by [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]], Ariel Rechtshaid, Kingdom, Girl Unit and Daniel Aged. It runs from the end of the relationship to the start.
years.xp:
Kelela announced the EP on March 3 with "A Message" and its video; "Rewind" followed on September 2. Pitchfork named it Best New Music, and Anupa Mistry called it a sensuous, sensitive, hi-definition approach to R&B.

According to Wikipedia it reached No. 4 on Billboard's Heatseekers and Top Dance Albums charts, and Fact ranked it No. 8 of 2015.

years.h: Solange, Danny Brown and Clams Casino all want her on their records
years.p: She sang on "Scales" from Solange's A Seat at the Table, "From the Ground" on Danny Brown's Atrocity Exhibition and "A Breath Away" on Clams Casino's 32 Levels.

years.h: Gorillaz put her on Humanz
years.p: Kelela sang on "Busted and Blue" for [[Gorillaz|e21857d5-3256-4547-afb3-4b6ded592596]], and joined Danny Brown on "Submission".

years.cap: Kelela on the Flog Stage at Camp Flog Gnaw, Los Angeles, 2017
years.src: Wikipedia: Take Me Apart · Wikipedia: Kelela
years.h: Four years later, Take Me Apart
years.p: Warp released the debut album on October 6, with [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]] and [[Jam City|1017c0b1-8219-4527-bc09-b32991bb8748]] behind most of it. Pitchfork gave it 8.6 and ranked it No. 4 of 2017.
years.xp:
It was recorded at Heavy Duty in Burbank and at Mutant and Rooftop in London, with Kwes mixing. The lead single "LMK" arrived August 1, and "Frontline" premiered on HBO's Insecure.

Metacritic has it at 84. Stereogum's Tom Breihan called it a towering achievement of an album, and it peaked at No. 128 on the Billboard 200, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: She stops and does the reading
eras.text: After the debut she did the reading. Remixers had to send stems, and collaborators on the next record got homework.

years.h: Remixers send stems, or they're not on the record
years.p: Kaytranada, Rare Essence and Serpentwithfeet reworked Take Me Apart, and a "LMK" remix pulled in Princess Nokia, Junglepussy, Cupcakke and Ms. Boogie.
years.xp: It came out exactly a year after the album. Kelela told Mixmag the rule: "Nothing is going to be on this project unless you're willing to send stems and allow me to do the final arrangement."

years.big: "There's a canon of approved Black sounds."
years.h: Collaborators get a reading list before a session
years.p: Kelela's primer of essays, podcasts and documentaries runs from Kandis Williams on misogynoir to Safiya Umoja Noble on algorithmic oppression. The quote is from her Rolling Stone interview.
years.xp:
Mixmag says the list was described as the "syllabus for the university of her mind" and that she sent it to her collaborators.

Rolling Stone asked her about the years after 2013. She called them a "post-Pitchfork era" and said the canon keeps expanding every year, with a hierarchical value system assigned to certain sounds. The only term she could come up with, she said, was sonic racism.

eras.title: Raven
eras.text: Six years after Take Me Apart, Kelela came back with a record built like a DJ set, made mostly in Berlin with the friends who had shaped her sound.

years.h: Most of Raven gets made in Berlin, 13 tracks in under two weeks
years.p: Kelela worked with OCA, Asmara Maroof of [[Nguzunguzu|de7d7191-5ca6-4e19-a69e-006a09a63df2]], [[LSDXOXO|c2710100-a9e9-46e9-bae7-4677333cd0eb]] and [[Bambii|6ca9bf1d-3992-4b77-84c9-90b88a8d0f10]]. The last track added was "Fooley", by Khalí Carela.
years.xp:
Kelela told Mixmag she found Carela's production online and told Carela to take it off Instagram: "I've never done this in my life." Asmara, a friend from her Maryland suburbs, was co-executive producer.

Wikipedia dates the recording to 2020 through 2022.

years.h: "Washed Away" is her first new single in five years
years.p: Kelela released the song with a video on September 13, 2022. Raven was announced on November 15, alongside "On the Run".

years.cap: Kelela at a London show on the Raven tour, spring 2023
years.h: Warp releases Raven, six years after her debut
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.4 and called it Best New Music, then ranked it No. 17 on its 50 Best Albums of 2023.
years.xp:
Eric Torres wrote in Pitchfork that it was a masterful display of tension and release. Metacritic has it at 86, and Resident Advisor put it at No. 1 for the year. Consequence had it at No. 13.

The 15 tracks run 62 minutes 33 seconds, with producers including Asmara, Yo van Lenz, LSDXOXO, Bambii, Kaytranada and Fauzia. "Contact" and "Enough for Love" were the last two singles.

Kelela told Rolling Stone the first half "feels like summer" and then the album carries you into the winter.

years.cap: Kelela on stage in London on the Raven tour, 2023
years.h: "Enough for Love" goes on Fallon the day Raven drops
years.p: Kelela performed the song on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon on February 10.

years.big: The space is dominated by Black men and light-skinned women.
years.h: Raven starts as a reaction to feeling alone
years.p: Kelela's press statement said the album grew out of being a Black femme working in dance music. She repeated the point to Mixmag.
years.xp:
Kelela told Mixmag she had privileges in that space, being thin and of Ethiopian descent.

The album runs its tracks together like a DJ set, moving through R&B, dancehall, drum 'n' bass and techno. In Rolling Stone she described the journey: "You run off the cliff in 'Contact,' and then you basically just dive deep into the depths of the ocean on 'Fooley.'"

years.h: PinkPantheress asks her to "Bury Me"
years.p: Kelela guests on "Bury Me" from [[PinkPantheress|7441014f-f8f5-494f-81db-ff166fbc078d]]'s debut album Heaven Knows.

eras.title: Blue Note, then guitars
eras.text: Raven kept going: a remix album, a Tiny Desk, a jazz-club residency, and a guitar-heavy third record with the songwriter behind PinkPantheress and Shygirl.

years.h: Twenty remixes of Raven, from Shygirl to Yaeji
years.p: Singles included Karen Nyame KG's "Contact" remix and Flexulant and Bambii's "Closure". Pitchfork gave the set 7.8.

years.h: NPR gives her a Tiny Desk
years.p: The Fader posted the Tiny Desk concert on February 23, 2024.

years.src: Wikipedia: In the Blue Light (Kelela album)
years.h: Two nights at New York's Blue Note Jazz Club
years.p: Her first residency there was recorded on May 28 and 29, with arrangements by bassist and producer [[Daniel Aged|db66224d-87de-4417-9a9d-afa43151ed72]].

years.src: Wikipedia: In the Blue Light (Kelela album) · Wikipedia: Kelela
years.h: In the Blue Light takes her songs unplugged, with harp and a jazz rhythm section
years.p: Warp released the live album from the Blue Note nights. It includes a cover of Joni Mitchell's "Furry Sings the Blues", and Pitchfork gave it 8.0.
years.xp:
The band was Daniel Aged on bass, Briley Harris on piano, Ahya Simone on harp and Buz Donald on drums, with Alayna Rodgers and Xenia Manasseh singing backup. Pitchfork's Tarisai Ngangura called her a masterful re-interpreter of her own songs.

"Better (Unplugged)" was the lead single on January 28, and a documentary film followed on February 18.

years.h: "Idea 1" is a grunge-guitar single written with Oscar Scheller
years.p: Her first single since Raven also credits painter Janiva Ellis as a writer, with shoegaze guitarist Scarlet House playing on it.

years.h: New Avatar is her third album on Warp
years.p: Mostly with Oscar Scheller, with A. K. Paul, Fousheé and PinkPantheress as guests. Metacritic has it at 85.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists "Outta Time", a duet with A. K. Paul that she says dates from the 2016 Take Me Apart sessions, and "The Bridge" with PinkPantheress as singles. Stereogum named it Album of the Week.

The New Avatar Live tour starts September 8, 2026, in Seattle.
